item.title: Caitlin Clark publicly questions Dallas Cowboys after embarrassing Thanksgiving loss
item.description: Credit: Ron Jenkins/Kevin C. Cox via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are getting criticised from all angles, and even WNBA superstar Caitlin Clark couldn’t resist questioning what went wrong on Thanksgiving. The Dallas Cowboys suffered one of the most embarrassing comeback losses at the hands of the Philadelphia Eagles on Thanksgiving Day. Despite having a 31-10 lead in the third quarter, they gave up nearly 30 points in the final quarter and a half to lose the game 39-38. The Cowboys’ misery was compounded by the fact that Philly was led by their own former player in Joe Milton III. The 26-year-old was on the same wavelength as DeVonta Smith, who had two touchdowns and 200 yards on the day. The entire situation naturally led to a lot of mockery and criticism for Dallas on social media, and even superstars from other leagues couldn’t resist. Caitlin Clark questions what the Cowboys were doing during their 4th quarter collapse Thanksgiving is all about the NFL when it comes to the world of sports, and the games have not disappointed in the slightest. That also means more people are tuned in than they are for the rest of the season. Caitlin Clark was also clearly watching this year. After the Cowboys fell apart in the fourth quarter, Clark was in disbelief much like the rest of the country, and she shared her bemusement on social media. “What exactly were the Cowboys doing there?” Clark asked in a post on X. She isn’t exactly known for posting regularly on the platform either, which just goes to show how wild what happened during the Dallas game was. This is unfortunately just the beginning for the 5-7 Cowboys. A loss like this doesn’t just go away, and especially not when it happens on a stage this big. There will be plenty of time for assessing everything that went wrong, but for now, Dallas will simply have to deal with all the mockery. item.title: ‘Hard to find the words’ – Alex Campos pens emotional message after making Barcelona debut
item.description: BAKU, AZERBAIJAN - NOVEMBER 25: Alex Campos of FC Barcelona runs with ball during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Sabah FC and FC Barcelona at Baku Olympic Stadium on November 25, 2026 in Baku, Azerbaijan. (Photo by Kazimierz Koper/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Alex Campos admits it’s “hard to find the words” to describe how he’s feeling after making his first-team debut for Barcelona in Wednesday’s Champions League win over Sabah. The center-back made his first appearance off the bench as Barcelona won 4-1 in Azerbaijan . Campos has now taken to social media to reveal just how much it means to him to play for the Catalan giants. “There are days you dream of experiencing since you were a child—days for which, when they finally arrive, it is hard to find the words to describe them,” he posted on Instagram. “Yesterday, I had the privilege of fulfilling one of those dreams: making my debut for the FC Barcelona first team in the Champions League. “Thank you to my family, teammates, coaches, and everyone who has been part of this journey and helped me get to where I am today. “Now, it’s time to keep working hard to earn more opportunities to experience moments like this—always with humility and dedication. Visca el Barça!” View this post on Instagram Campos will certainly be hoping for more chances throughout the season. The defender has been with the squad for the last few games, due to injuries to Hansi Flick’s backline, and certainly didn’t look out of place after arriving for the last 25 minutes or so.

item.title: Caitlin Clark Calls Out Cowboys With 7-Word Reaction to Dallas’ Thanksgiving Choke Job vs. Eagles
item.description: Chiefs fan Caitlin Clark questions the Cowboys after Dallas blows a 21-point lead in a Thanksgiving loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark had a one-line question for the Dallas Cowboys after their 39-38 Thanksgiving loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. Dallas let a 21-point lead slip away at AT&T Stadium, with Jake Elliott winning it for Philadelphia on a 59-yard field goal with two seconds left. The Eagles also had an unexpected contributor in quarterback Joe Milton, who started against his former team after joining Philadelphia from Dallas’ practice squad in October. Chiefs Fan Caitlin Clark Has a Question for the Cowboys After Thanksgiving Collapse The three-time WNBA All-Star has long supported the Kansas City Chiefs, who also played on Thanksgiving, but her attention turned to the Cowboys-Eagles game. She wrote : “What exactly were the Cowboys doing there?” Clark didn’t specify which moment prompted the question. Clark has made her NFL loyalties clear before, including during an appearance on Kylie Kelce’s podcast earlier this month. On the November 3 episode of “Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce,” host Kylie Kelce brought up the Colts jersey Clark had passed on wearing, despite the Fever sharing Indianapolis with the NFL team. Clark said she hadn’t initially thought about upsetting Chiefs fans or Travis Kelce by wearing the jersey. However, she realized afterward that her teammates had worn theirs. She put it plainly : “I am diehard Chiefs. I’ve been diehard since I was a young kid and it is what it is.” Kelce also asked whether Travis Kelce ranked above every other Chiefs player in Clark’s eyes. The Fever guard named him her favorite, with Patrick Mahomes right behind him. She also mentioned former Kansas City tight end Tony Gonzalez as a player she admired growing up. Back in Arlington, the Cowboys appeared to have control of the game after building a 31-10 lead in the third quarter. Milton, who had previously served as Philadelphia’s third-string quarterback, helped lead the comeback. He threw for 331 yards and 3 touchdowns, including two scoring passes to DeVonta Smith. He also ran for a 15-yard touchdown in the fourth quarter. The Eagles started their comeback when Ty Robinson blocked Bryan Anger’s punt, allowing Kenny Moore II to recover the ball and return it 3 yards for a touchdown. Dak Prescott answered with a 14-yard touchdown run, restoring Dallas’ 14-point advantage at 38-24. Milton responded with his rushing score, and the Eagles continued to chip away at the deficit. item.title: Christian Mahogany, Dan Campbell Address Costly Taunting Penalty in Detroit Lions Loss to Bears
item.description: For a moment, it looked like Jahmyr Gibbs had delivered the knockout blow in the Detroit Lions’ Thanksgiving Day matchup against the Chicago Bears. With 8:20 remaining in the fourth quarter, Gibbs exploded for a 70-yard touchdown run that put the Lions in position to take a 12-point lead. Unfortunately, what happened immediately after the touchdown proved costly. Lions offensive lineman Christian Mahogany was flagged for taunting, resulting in a 15-yard penalty that pushed Jake Bates’ extra-point attempt back to 48 yards. Bates missed the kick, and what could have been a relatively insignificant penalty ended up having a major impact on how the remainder of the game unfolded. Christian Mahogany Takes Responsibility for Costly Penalty Following Detroit’s 39-35 loss to Chicago, Mahogany acknowledged that he allowed Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons to get under his skin. Rather than making excuses for his actions, Mahogany admitted that he failed to keep his emotions in check. “I feel bad that that happened,” Mahogany told reporters in the locker room. “I just got too hot and too high and let my emotions get the best of me.” Mahogany’s comments came on the same afternoon that he accused the Bears of simulating Jared Goff’s snap count . Clearly, there was no love lost between Mahogany and Simmons throughout Thursday’s divisional showdown. Detroit Lions’ head coach Dan Campbell looks over plan with defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard during the first half of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Ford Field in Detroit on Thanksgiving Day, Nov. 26, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dan Campbell Explains How Mahogany’s Penalty Changed the Game During his postgame press conference, Lions head coach Dan Campbell explained why the missed extra point was so significant. The difference between an 11-point lead and a 12-point lead fundamentally changed the decisions both teams faced down the stretch. “It changed the dynamic of the points, because now you’re going for two instead of just kicking a field goal, and now it changes the end of that game,” Campbell said, as also reported by NFL.com . According to the game recap from Pride of Detroit , Chicago responded by marching 71 yards in just three plays, capped off by a Rome Odunze touchdown reception. The Bears converted the ensuing two-point attempt, cutting Detroit’s lead to 35-32 rather than 36-32. item.description: Dallas Cowboys QB Dak Prescott. Getty Have yourself a Thanksgiving Day, Dak Prescott. The Dallas Cowboys quarterback thrilled AT&T Stadium and the football-watching world by leaving his feet for a soaring touchdown, capping a 14-yard run and giving his team a 38-24 lead with 10:11 left in the fourth quarter on Thursday against the Philadelphia Eagles. item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 26: Patrick Mahomes #15 of the Kansas City Chiefs drops back to pass while being pressured by Greg Rousseau #15 of the Buffalo Bills in the second quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Joe Hrycych/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau moved into a tie for seventh place on the team’s all-time sacks list on Thanksgiving night. Rousseau sacked quarterback Patrick Mahomes on a 3rd & 16 midway through the third quarter on Thanksgiving night to bring his career total to 43, catching former Bills defensive end Mario Williams. Greg Rousseau tallies his 11th sack of the season 💪 KCvsBUF on NBC/Peacock Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hBKaqwPgjQ — NFL (@NFL) November 27, 2026 Williams spent four seasons (2012-2015) in Buffalo, recording double-digit sacks in each of his first three years with the team. His best season came in 2014 when he recorded 14.5 sacks and earned first-team All-Pro honors. Rousseau, now in his sixth NFL season, has spent his entire career in Buffalo after the Bills selected him with the 30th overall pick in the 2021 NFL Draft. Having already established a new personal single-season record for sacks this year , the 26 year old is now working his way through some familiar names in Buffalo’s history books. Once Rousseau gets past Mario Williams, there’s another Williams waiting for him. Former defensive tackle Kyle Williams (48.5), who spent all 13 of his NFL seasons in Buffalo, sits sixth on the franchise’s all-time list. With six regular-season games remaining, and the way Rousseau has been getting to opposing quarterbacks lately, we might not have to wait until next season to talk about him catching another Williams.

item.title: ‘Please Don’t Get It Done,’ ‘Everybody Hates Him’ — CFB Fans React to ESPN Being ‘Not Close to an Agreement’ With Kirk Herbstreit Over New Contract
item.description: ‘Please Don’t Get It Done,’ ‘Everybody Hates Him’ — CFB Fans React to ESPN Being ‘Not Close to an Agreement’ With Kirk Herbstreit Over New Contract ESPN pushed back Wednesday on a Front Office Sports report by Ryan Glasspiegel that the network was nearing a long-term extension with Kirk Herbstreit, its lead college football analyst. Herbstreit’s ESPN contract runs out once this college football season ends, and the network’s response pointed to fuller talks after the season, with ESPN hoping to land a new deal then. Fans who weighed in on the news Thursday, however, showed little appetite for a new contract at all, and several wanted ESPN to move on. ESPN Eyes Kirk Herbstreit Talks After the College Football Season ESPN’s statement cooled talk that a deal was near. “We’re not close to an agreement,” a spokesperson for the network told Front Office Sports. “We have communicated to Kirk’s team that we are prepared to engage more directly after the college football season, and we’re hopeful we can get something done at that time.” Herbstreit did not immediately get back to Front Office Sports when it asked for comment. ESPN’s timeline matches what Andrew Marchand reported in September: that ESPN would hold off on talks with Herbstreit until the offseason. Herbstreit joined the College GameDay cast in 1996 and took over as the network’s lead college football game analyst in 2006. With the win, the No. 7 Longhorns (7-0) advance to face Saint Mary's in the championship game on Friday at 4 p.m. Johnson left early in Sunday's win over Southern Indiana with a pain in his "butt," according to head coach Sean Miller. item.title: James Cook makes NFL history on Thanksgiving night
item.description: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 26: James Cook III #4 of the Buffalo Bills runs with the ball while being chased by Mansoor Delane #5 of the Kansas City Chiefs in the second quarter at Highmark Stadium on November 26, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has a share of another NFL record. Cook has now rushed for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in 10 consecutive games, tying a record Terry Allen set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons with Washington. James Cook III has now rushed for 75+ yards and a TD in 10 consecutive games, extending his record for the longest single-season streak in NFL history. pic.twitter.com/TbTrvIPiQb — Buffalo Bills PR (@BuffaloBillsPR) November 27, 2026 Cook found the end zone against the Kansas City Chiefs on Thanksgiving night during the second quarter to put the Bills up 7-0 . He then eclipsed the 75-yard mark in the third quarter on a five-yard run that put him at 79 for the night. JIMBO!!! 📺: NBC pic.twitter.com/83xqEMHxZ8 — Buffalo Bills (@BuffaloBills) November 27, 2026 It’s been 30 years since Allen put together his streak of 10 games. Since then, we’ve watched some pretty impressive running backs come through the NFL. LaDainian Tomlinson, Adrian Peterson, and Derrick Henry have all had their share of record-setting performances, but none of them managed to do what Cook just did. And unlike Allen, who needed parts of two seasons to put together his streak, Cook has done it all in the same season. In fact, the Bills’ season opener was the only game this year in which Cook didn’t meet both statistical requirements. Cook entered Thursday night’s game having rushed for 1,003 yards and 10 touchdowns over the course of his nine-game streak, averaging 111.4 yards per game and 5.1 yards per carry. He eclipsed the century mark in five of those nine games, including a season-high 157-yard performance against the New York Jets. Remember when we spent so much of the offseason in 2025 talking about whether the Bills should pay Cook? Buffalo eventually gave its running back a four-year, $48 million contract extension, and Cook has spent the better part of two seasons giving us reasons to talk about what a good decision that was. The Bills will head to Foxborough next week for their second meeting of the season with the New England Patriots. Cook rushed for 75 yards and a touchdown on 12 carries in their first matchup. Another 75 yards and a trip to the end zone next week, and Cook will have an NFL record all to himself. Considering we’ve been watching him do just that every week since September, it might be time to start wondering just how big a number he’s going to leave for the next running back to chase.

item.title: Skip Bayless says what he ‘feared’ about Joe Milton actually came true during Cowboys vs Eagles
item.description: Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images Philadelphia Eagles star Joe Milton was the star of the show in his first game against his old team, the Dallas Cowboys. The quarterback was demoted to the practice squad by Dallas after an underwhelming pre-season. The Eagles picked him up, and his recent performances have made that decision look like a masterstroke. Milton was outstanding on Thanksgiving in the 39-38 comeback win for Philadelphia, and Skip Bayless has now claimed that he saw this coming. Skip Bayless says he feared Joe Milton would come back to haunt the Dallas Cowboys Milton had a fantastic game against the Dallas Cowboys. The 26-year-old had impressed in his first two starts against the Giants and the Steelers, but he didn’t manage a single touchdown pass in those appearances. However, against his old team, he scored four total scores on Thanksgiving and was one of the best players on the field. Bayless was hoping that Milton would not come back to haunt the Cowboys, but his worst fears came true, and Dallas ended up losing despite leading for most of the game. The TV presenter said in a video on X: “I did say on Friday’s Gridiron, I feared Joe Milton. He’s Josh Allen. He’s 6’5″, 240, ran 4’6”, coming out of Tennessee, and he’s got a huge arm. It was just sensational.” Bayless posted a series of tweets during the game, and he showered Milton with praise, comparing him to Josh Allen and claiming that the quarterback was ‘torching the team that demoted him’. The Eagles star finished the game with 21 of 31 passes completed for 331 yards, three passing touchdowns and an interception, while adding 15 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown. It’s still early days for Milton, who has only started three games, but the signs are really positive, and he could make a big difference for the Eagles if he continues playing in the same way. item.title: Beckham Black, No. 1 Basketball Recruit, Cancels Duke Visit
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Beckham Black ’s recruitment took another turn Tuesday, with the five-star guard no longer expected to make a scheduled visit to Duke. Black, the No. 1 overall prospect in the 2027 Rivals Industry Rankings, had been expected to attend the Blue Devils’ Nov. 17 matchup against Illinois. The visit was removed from his schedule, according to Jon Van Hoozer of High School On SI . No reason for the cancellation was reported, and there is no indication that Black has ruled out Duke. For now, it is a change to his recruiting itinerary, not necessarily a shift in his list of contenders. Black Has Visited Several National Powers Black has already taken visits to Texas, North Carolina, Florida, Arkansas and Georgetown, according to Rivals. That list features some of the biggest names in college basketball, with programs from the SEC, ACC and Big East getting an opportunity to make their pitch to the five-star prospect. Duke was next on the schedule. The cancellation leaves the Blue Devils without that planned opportunity, but it does not tell the full story of where they stand in his recruitment. Black remains one of the top uncommitted players in the 2027 class, and his next recruiting move will be worth watching as his senior season progresses. Black’s Production at Southeastern Prep Speaks for Itself While the recruiting picture remains unsettled, Black has been putting up big numbers at Southeastern Prep in Orlando. The school lists him at 21.1 points, 6.5 rebounds and 9.4 assists per game through 11 appearances. He has shown the ability to take over as a scorer while also creating opportunities for his teammates. Black poured in 33 points and dished out nine assists in a 78-77 win over Prince George’s Christian on Nov. 13. A day later, he recorded 15 points, 11 rebounds and nine assists in an 80-65 victory against Cats Academy. He also posted 20 points and 20 assists against the Diamond Doves earlier in November. On Oct. 30, Black delivered one of his biggest performances of the season, finishing with 45 points, 13 rebounds and 10 assists against BC Dubai. Those numbers show why Black is viewed as one of the premier prospects in the country. He can score at a high level, but his playmaking makes him an even more difficult matchup. Black Has Built a National Profile Black’s résumé extends beyond his high school production. He has won two gold medals with USA Basketball and is the younger brother of NBA guard Anthony Black. Originally from Duncanville, Texas, he has continued to build his profile at Southeastern Prep. Rivals reported that Black averaged 21.7 points, 5.4 assists, four rebounds and 1.7 steals on the EYBL circuit over the summer. For now, his college destination remains unknown. Duke’s canceled visit adds another wrinkle to a recruitment that already includes several prominent programs, but Black’s next decision will offer a clearer picture of where things stand. item.description: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Joe Milton (14) smiles as he talks with Fox’s Tom Rinaldi after winning an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington. (Elías Valverde II/The Dallas Morning News) ARLINGTON — Eagles backup quarterback Joe Milton was smiling when he met the media late Thursday afternoon. Milton completed 21 of 31 passes for 331 yards with three touchdowns and one interception in the Eagles' dramatic 39-38 victory over the Cowboys . For Milton, it wasn’t a time to gloat, considering he spent nearly two seasons with the Cowboys as a backup quarterback. But it was hard not to notice the smile. “I know that defense like the back of my hand,” Milton said. Dallas Cowboys fans Liza Cruz holds hands with her daughter Ashley Adauto as they record a video dressed as turkeys before an NFL football game against the Philadelphia Eagles at AT&T Stadium on Thursday, Nov. 26, 2026, in Arlington. The only thing you can do is just prepare yourself and that’s just the main thing I did.” Milton got his revenge, leading a six-play, 11-yard drive that took 48 seconds to set up kicker Jake Elliott for a game-winning 59-yard field goal with seven seconds to play. It was part of a 22-point fourth quarter where Milton completed 8 of 13 passes for 111 yards with a touchdown pass and a touchdown run. The Cowboys led 31-17 to start the fourth quarter before the Eagles' rally. He exchanged messages with quarterback Dak Prescott and other players during the season. The biggest thing Milton had to overcome was finding a touch on some passes. He knew the offense, it was just controlling his arm strength. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class.
